name: contempt
description: A feeling of dislike-for and superiority-over another person, group of people, and/or their actions.

variations.name: contempt from group
variations.description: Dislike for a person stemming from their perceived group membership.

variations.name: contempt for a behavior
variations.description: Scorn for someone who does something that goes against a principle you deem important.

variations.name: status from tearing others down
variations.description: Emphasizing someone else's behavior to distract attention about your own behavior.

variations.name: contempt from pity
variations.description: The sense that another person must deserve their misfortune because of some failing.

variations.name: contempt for the unusual
variations.description: A sense that another person is different from others in a bad way.

commentaries.quote: We accuse others of what we cannot accept in ourselves.
Contempt is a way to signal to someone that we're higher status than them in some characteristic. And it's a way to communicate to everyone listening which characteristics we value.
For most of us, contempt is easier than compassion.

conditions: A negative judgment about someone's characteristics that puts the self in a superior position.
